To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the freeze-thaw, osmo- sis, and chemical lysis methods are suitable for the determination of total platinum in lysates of in vitro cultured human malignant cells exposed in vitro to cisplatin.

osmosis is the most suitable lysis method for determination of cisplatin metabolites in human malignant cells, and that freeze-thaw and chemical detergent-based lysis methods can be used for determination of total platinum concentration in cells.

osmosis is the best method of lysing human malignant cells for the analysis of platinum metallomes, and that the chemical detergent lysis method is the most effective method for the determination and quantification of cisplatin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of analytical methods for the characterization of platinum drug metabolite profiles in malignant cells.

the development of a metallomic methodology for the analysis of platinum compounds and their metabolites in biological samples, and here we have demonstrated a method for cell lysis of human malignant cells exposed in vitro to the platinum anticancer drug cisplatin.
the development and application of metallomic methods for the analysis of platinum compounds in human malignant cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all the lysis methods are equally suitable for the determination of total platinum content in human malignant cells exposed in vitro to cisplatin.

all three lysis methods evaluated are suitable for the quantification of total intracellular platinum concentration, and the osmosis method is recommended for the analysis of reactive platinum compounds.
all three cell lysis methods can be recommended for platinum metallomic analysis, but that the chemical lysis method is not suitable for metallome profiling of reactive platinum analytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the freeze-thaw, osmotically induced lysis, and the chemical detergent-based lysis methods can be used for the determination of total platinum in human malignant cells, but the chemical detergent-based method cannot be recommended for analysis of reactive and unknown analytes.
the chemical lysis method was the best for the determination of nonreactive platinum compounds and the osmosis method the best for the analysis of reactive platinum compounds.

, in general, the chemical lysis method is the best for the determination of total platinum concentration in lysate, whereas the osmosis method is the best method for the determination and identification of intracellular cisplatin and cisplatin metabolites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for metallomic studies of platinum in malignant cells exposed to platinum drugs, it is important to use a cell lysis method with a known effect on platinum compounds of interest.
the choice of cell lysis method can significantly impact metallomic studies.
the cell lysis procedure should be chosen with consideration of the analytical method to be applied.
